Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Is there one test of a prophet all could accept?

The Torah's two tests of a prophet: does his word come true, whom does he call to? Here, a tool for any book.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَـٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدْ جَآءَكُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ وَإِن يَكُ كَـٰذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُۥ ۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allāh' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allāh does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.

Quran · Ghafir 40:28

A shared test should come from a book the parties already honour. The Torah, in Deuteronomy, gives one: if someone speaks in God's name and what he says does not come to pass, God did not speak it. That rule can be checked. This verse is said by a man of Pharaoh's household, pleading for a threatened messenger. He weighs it the same way: if he lies, that falls on him; if he is truthful, some of it will reach you. Let the outcome speak.

A question for you

What makes a prediction count as a real test?

If you sayIt is specific and stated in advance.
ThenThat is a strong standard. A vague word can fit any outcome, which calls for care with the prophecies of every tradition.
If you sayIt could have turned out otherwise.
ThenThat is the heart of it. A claim that cannot fail cannot be confirmed either.
If you sayPredictions prove nothing. Anyone can get lucky.
ThenOne hit can be luck. That is why this test gives a minimum and not a verdict. The second test asks something else.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We sent not before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:25

Translation

I am Yahweh, and there is no one else. Besides me, there is no God. I will strengthen you, though you have not known me,

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד זוּלָתִ֖י אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲאַזֶּרְךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽנִי׃

Isaiah · 45:5

World English Bible

﴿وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَـٰحِرٍ ۖ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is."

Quran · Ta-Ha 20:69

Deuteronomy adds a harder case. Suppose the sign does come true, but the one who gave it calls people to other gods. Then he is not to be followed, because a wonder does not outrank the call to God alone. So the test has two parts: what comes to pass, and to whom the speaker calls. The first verse here states this as the message of every messenger: none is to be served but the One. A wonder can impress anyone. What counts is what it is used for.

A question for you

If a wonder and a message pull in different directions, which would you follow?

If you sayThe message.
ThenThen a wonder alone would not move you, which means stories of wonders cannot be your main evidence in any tradition.
If you sayThe wonder. It is at least evidence.
ThenIt is evidence that something happened. What it shows about the message is the open question, and both books slow down at that point.
If you sayNeither, until I know more.
ThenA fair place to stand. Both tests ask you to wait and look.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِۦ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur’ān, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."

Quran · Al-Isra 17:88

﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down [i.e., the Qur’ān] upon Our Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)], then produce a sūrah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses [i.e., supporters] other than Allāh, if you should be truthful.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:23

A test is fair only if you would apply it to what you already hold. So use it evenly: on the prophets of your own tradition, on those of others, and on this book. Ask of any text: what did it stake in advance that could fail? The first verse here stakes something: that all who try will not produce its like. Weighing that is left to you, and it takes Arabic or those who know it. No tradition is given a verdict here. You have been given the tool.

A question for you

On what would this test be hardest for you to use?

If you sayMy own tradition.
ThenThen you have found where the test is worth the most. It asks nothing of you tonight.
If you sayA tradition I have already dismissed.
ThenFairness to what you have dismissed can be harder than honesty about what you love. It is also what makes the result worth anything.
If you sayThis book.
ThenA reasonable place to start, and the book itself invites it.

The same in the other books
